To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adsorption of cellulase on indigo is much higher than on cellulose and that the best washing performance of the enzyme is associated with its ability to bind indigo.
the adsorption of several purified cellulases on indigo particles was much higher than on Avicel cellululose, and the enzyme adsorption was less specific than on cellulose.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new approach to the study of enzyme--substrate interaction, and the results obtained may be useful in the design of more efficient cellulases for the enzymatic denim washing process.
the identification of the structural features of the enzyme molecule that determine its adsorption and catalytic properties in the process of indigo decolorization.
the identification of protein--indigo interaction domains in cellulase molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of hydrophobic amino acid residues in a protein molecule, especially in the vicinity of its active centre, may be a necessary, but not a sufficient condition for its ability to bind to indigo particles.
the adsorption of cellulase molecules on indigo particles occurs through the interaction sites that are located on the surface of cellulases, but are not involved in the hydrolysis of cellulose.
the adsorption of enzymes on indigo is not only a physical process but also a chemical interaction of the enzyme with the dye molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cellulases with a higher content of hydrophobes on their surface are more efficient in removing indigo from denim than cellulases with less hydrophobes.
the indigo adsorption on cellulases is a good model of the adsorption of these enzymes on the cellulose fibers of denim fabric.

cellulase molecules with a larger number of hydrophobic amino acid residues in their surface regions, which are able to bind indigo molecules, have a better washing performance in the enzymatic denim treatment process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of indigo-binding sites on the surface of cellulases is an important factor determining the efficiency of indigo removal from the denim fabric.
the presence of indigo-binding sites in cellulase enzymes can be detected by the measurement of enzyme adsorption on the indigo-containing substrate.
the adsorption on indigotin (indigo) is not a good indicator of cellulolytic activity of the enzyme.
